claim: Pandu SUGGESTS_PRINCIPLE Oleation with medicated ghee (snehana) in Pandu
statement: Medicated ghee is given for oleation to persons with Pandu and Kamala.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Pandu SUGGESTS_PRINCIPLE Purification (saṃśodhana) with sharp emetic and purgative drugs after oleation, in Pandu
statement: A person with Pandu, after oleation, is to be purified with sharp drugs acting upwards and downwards (emesis and purgation).
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Pandu SUGGESTS_PRINCIPLE Wholesome diet (pathya) after purification, in Pandu
statement: After purification, wholesome foods are to be given.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Pandu SUGGESTS_PRINCIPLE Medication chosen according to the predominant dosha, in Pandu
statement: Specific medicines are to be given according to the dosha involved.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Wholesome diet (pathya) after purification, in Pandu RECOMMENDS_DIET Old śāli rice, barley and wheat with soups
statement: The wholesome diet consists of old śāli rice, barley and wheat taken with soups.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Wholesome diet (pathya) after purification, in Pandu RECOMMENDS_DIET Soups of mung bean, pigeon pea and lentil
statement: Soups of mung bean, pigeon pea and lentil are part of the wholesome diet.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Wholesome diet (pathya) after purification, in Pandu RECOMMENDS_DIET Meat soups of dry-land (jāṅgala) animals
statement: Meat soups of dry-land animals are described as beneficial in the wholesome diet.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Wholesome diet (pathya) after purification, in Pandu RECOMMENDS_DIET Water boiled with the sthirādi group of drugs, for drinking and cooking
statement: Water boiled with the sthirādi drugs is praised for drinking and food for persons with Pandu (grape and āmalakī juice is given for Kamala in the same verse).
ai_note: Verse continues into Ca.6.16.115; which drink is meant for Pandu and which for Kamala depends on reading across the verse boundary.

claim: Oleation with medicated ghee (snehana) in Pandu USES_FORMULATION Kalyāṇaka ghṛta
statement: Kalyāṇaka ghṛta is one of the ghees named for oleation in Pandu and Kamala.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Oleation with medicated ghee (snehana) in Pandu USES_FORMULATION Pañcagavya ghṛta

claim: Oleation with medicated ghee (snehana) in Pandu USES_FORMULATION Mahātikta ghṛta

claim: Oleation with medicated ghee (snehana) in Pandu USES_FORMULATION Dāḍimādya ghṛta
statement: Dāḍimādya ghṛta is described as alleviating heart disease, Pandu, gulma, piles and spleen disorders.
ai_note: Quote supports Dadimadya ghrta as curative in Pandu; placing it under the oleation principle is an inference from context.

claim: Purification (saṃśodhana) with sharp emetic and purgative drugs after oleation, in Pandu USES_HERB Harītakī
statement: Harītakī soaked in cow's urine is given as a purgative in kaphaja Pandu.
ai_note: The quoted source passage states the claim.

claim: Medication chosen according to the predominant dosha, in Pandu USES_FORMULATION Śilājatu vaṭaka

claim: Medication chosen according to the predominant dosha, in Pandu USES_FORMULATION Punarnavā maṇḍūra

ai_note: Quote supports the classical preparation; modern evidence that milk inhibits non-heme iron absorption is kept as a qualification.
